note: Bug cases undo a real fix from cedia's history (src only, tests left out), so the change under review brings the bug back. key is the one-sentence answer: a finding earns credit only when it names that defect. Controls replay a commit that stayed clean; every finding on one is a false alarm.

bugs.key: The read-only check no longer applies bash's backslash rule, so escaped flags like `sed \-i` or `sort -\o` pass as read-only while bash runs them as writes.
The browser checks for private addresses only when the host is a literal IP, so a name that resolves to a private or metadata address (169.254.169.254.nip.io) is opened.
grep over a directory above a credential store (e.g. $HOME) is no longer denied, so it reads ~/.kube/config, ~/.docker/config.json and similar secrets.
The policy expands ~ to home while the file tools read ~ as a folder under the working directory, so a path like ~/../../.ssh/config is judged one way and opened another.
All calls of a reply are decided before any runs, so a later call is judged against a tree an earlier call (e.g. a symlink) has since changed, escaping the workspace.
Repository and detected checks become bash allow rules for read-only sessions, so a repo check of "*" grants bash(*) to plan, review and explore sessions.
Every nonzero bash exit (a grep with no match, a failing test) and any 5xx number in output is counted as a tool error.
The read-only check misses bundled short flags and script files (sed -ni, sort -uo, sed -f, tree -fo), so commands that write pass as read-only.
A plugin name or team id is joined into a path unchecked, so '../keep' or '../settings' reaches outside the plugins or teams directory.
cedia serve listens on all interfaces with no authentication and runs any POST /run prompt with workspace access and no sandbox.
sleep ignores the abort signal and Monitor keeps every line unbounded in memory and in its result.
Settings writers fall back to {} when settings.json fails to parse and write that back, losing every other setting, and skip validation.
ultrareview keeps findings on files the change never touched, because its passes skip verifyFindings.
git, gh, rg and ffmpeg that cedia runs itself inherit process.env whole, so a repository hook or credential helper can read the provider API keys.
